resources.name: Build on Care
resources.learned: CARE supplies patients, encounters, forms, scheduling and organisational structure. Build one focused frontend/backend/integration extension rather than a separate general EMR.
resources.implication: Possible clinician-side host for Sahara; it does not automatically connect the existing app.
resources.boundary: Page recommends synthetic data, permission testing and further clinical/security/privacy validation.

resources.name: How to Build Healthcare Apps on CARE
resources.coverage: Opened in Chrome; read public transcript through 02:08, visible summary/chapters and selected later plugin/video-consultation demonstration frames/captions. Full transcript is gated by signup. Not claimed as a complete verbatim video review.
resources.learned: Separates CARE core from extensions; shows platform clinical/operational capabilities, palliative/home-care use and a video-consultation extension demonstration.
resources.boundary: No Loom account created and no authentication or transcript gate bypassed. Auto-summary transcribes CARE as CAD; use the official CARE spelling.

resources.name: Plugin system
resources.coverage: Read official architecture and development guide
resources.learned: Backend plugins are Django apps registered through PlugManager; frontend Care Apps are federated React bundles exposing a manifest. Extensions can be frontend-only, backend-only or both.
resources.implication: A Kotlin screen cannot directly load the React plugin contract; use a deliberate API/auth integration or a separate CARE clinician UI.
resources.boundary: Pin the target host contract and version; local in-tree development differs from production remote-entry loading. The guide's extra care_scribe example link returned 404 during this check.

resources.name: Care scaffold
resources.coverage: Read README, bootstrap and architecture/auth guidance
resources.learned: Isolated development workspace plus Django backend and React/TypeScript/Vite frontend templates. Plugin owns models, migrations, API and UI without requiring a CARE core fork.
resources.boundary: Guidance inspected as source material; bootstrap and skills were not installed/executed. CARE staff JWT and patient OTP are separate scopes; Sahara's existing authentication is not automatically compatible.

resources.name: OHC AI coding skills
resources.coverage: Read developer skill inventory and key instructions
resources.learned: Developer aids for CARE code review, questionnaire JSON, Jinja reports, SQL review and Playwright verification. They are not clinical models or delivered patient features.
resources.boundary: Validate generated forms against the actual host schema; examples/default conventions are not fully consistent. No skill was installed.

resources.name: Care Filly
resources.coverage: Read current default README, endpoint, client and licence
resources.learned: Current default is a Medispeak session-token broker. It authenticates CARE users, checks facility permissions and retains the long-lived provider key on the server while issuing short-lived scoped sessions.
resources.boundary: The main branch describes an older Sarvam/Groq/OpenAI architecture; it is not the current default implementation. Audio travels to Medispeak, not only to the device. Sarvam sponsorship does not confer Medispeak access. Filly has an MIT LICENSE.

resources.name: Care AI Vision
resources.coverage: Read current default README, manifest, OCR/session client and confidence prompt
resources.learned: React CARE extension fills registration/lab-report fields from documents using Filly-scoped Medispeak sessions, with user review and low-confidence flags.
resources.boundary: Requires CARE host/auth/facility and Medispeak access. Model-reported 0.99 confidence is not measured 99% accuracy. Default frontend sends document modality but current Filly does not forward it: source-level protocol concern, not a reproduced runtime failure. A manifest MIT declaration is not a blanket repository licence verification.

extraPrimarySource.title: CARE Home Care Grid

extraPrimarySource.evidenceLimit: Provider's platform/deployment account, not an independent audit or a Sahara partnership.

subsequentImplementation.relationshipToOriginalAudit: The scope, context, resources, delivery gap list and recommendation above are preserved as the original dated static audit. The following update records work completed after that audit. Use this mapping for the native 0.5 candidate; do not read the earlier native-gap descriptions as the current implementation state.
subsequentImplementation.deliveryStatus: 104 unit tests across 16 suites passed, debug lint 0 errors/37 warnings and vital release task passed. Signed unchanged-source 0.5.0 (6) uploaded once and saved as Alpha release 4 Draft; Production 0.4.1 review preserved. 35 latest passing Android test identities and one expected credential-dependent skip across six runs of unchanged original app code; not a single clean 36-test run. Exact-version publish/persistence, Privacy after actual Saved snackbar dismissal, optimized IME/restart and doctor publication/PDF/exit stages passed. Separate five-page/130-line PDF passed. No real speech/provider, physical-device or 16 KB runtime validation.

delivery.status: Combined source built and unit-checked; current-source manual-source/consent persistence and local-only consent guards passed, actual speech-service behavior unverified
delivery.implemented: Existing phone-private recording/replay remains. On supported Android 12+ phones, optional on-device turn dictation records the selected Patient, Family / carer or Doctor label, selected language and timestamp with editable words. Each turn requires microphone consent. Lifecycle and generation guards stop listening and reject late callbacks; no cloud speech fallback is configured.
delivery.remaining: The selected speaker is self-entered, not automatically identified or verified. Saved M4A recordings are not automatically transcribed. Language availability and speech accuracy depend on the installed on-device service and have not been validated in this emulator run.

delivery.status: Exact excerpt assignment implemented; generative draft remains unconnected
delivery.implemented: Users assign exact source lines to care-note sections and inspect the original words from each saved version. Changed wording has no exact citation. Repeated wording exposes every matching source line instead of claiming one uniquely identified speaker. The existing explicit-heading organiser remains available and preserves negation and uncertainty.
delivery.remaining: This is a reviewed excerpt workflow, not an AI summary. No Sarvam or other generative source-to-summary model, automatic saved-audio transcription, translation or clinically validated draft generation is connected. The merged upstream developer transcription path is retained behind release-disabled cloud-audio guards; its presence does not enable clinical audio or establish a provider deployment.

delivery.area: Native calendar and numeric lab history
delivery.status: Current-source debug persistence and person-isolation checks passed; optimized Calendar/Care team/Labs saves above actual IME and process-restart persistence passed
delivery.implemented: The calendar uses actual dated medicines, visits, tests, procedures, follow-ups, requests and tasks; undated medicines are separate and no recurrence is invented. Lab history keeps numeric values, report dates, exact units, optional report links and copied printed limits. Incompatible units are separate series. High/Low labels compare only explicit numeric limits for that result; textual or age-specific range text is not interpreted. Switching people keeps records isolated. Calendar, lab and care-team editors use the existing fully expanded sheet pattern. Actual optimized-release IME/window evidence verifies their save controls above the keyboard; selected debug images were inspected at 384 dp without OS overlays. This is CI emulator evidence, not physical-device verification.

qualifiedCanvaFindings.title: CARE HMIS
qualifiedCanvaFindings.capture: Real Chrome opened the public presentation. All 56 captured slide text bodies were read; 56 JPEGs were preserved, 31 selected images inspected and eight render-lag pairings identified. The earlier unsupported-client response remains an initial fetch attempt, not the current deck-access state.
qualifiedCanvaFindings.mediaLimit: Observed embedded sources were session-only blob references. A supported downloadMedia() call on a loaded visible video returned 'Blob downloads are not supported by this browser.' No raw embedded clip, full playback/audio review or 56 matched rendered text/image pairs are claimed.
qualifiedCanvaFindings.lessons: The deck emphasizes connected care workflows, standard codes and units, existing CarePlan/Goal/Consent concepts, and clinician review of AI drafts. CARE already presents palliative, home-care and oncology use cases; Sahara's proposed distinction is attributable reviewed goals-of-care continuity. Filly, record summaries, document extraction and timeline-based discharge drafts are provider capability examples, not proof they are integrated or clinically validated in Sahara. Deployment totals and screenshots remain provider claims.

palliativeFindings.finding: CARE Home Care Grid already covers registries, caregivers, assignments, home visits, goals/care plans, referrals, follow-ups and programme dashboards. Do not present a generic palliative registry as a capability absent from CARE. Deployment counts remain OHC's dated provider claims.
OHC already describes procedure/data-sharing consent, voice-assisted documentation and printable summaries. These are not unique Sahara inventions.

The playbook calls for caregiver capture, shared patient matching and palliative goals of care separate from acute notes. Its programme-enrollment flow is marked coming soon; an intended playbook is not proof every step is shipped.

Consent includes DNR, advance directives and a backend comfort-care category. Current docs flag comfort-care selection and patient/family verification UI as gaps. These data fields do not establish legal validity.

CARE can store Family/Validation verification, but documentation says its current web UI cannot add/show/remove it. Backend staff attribution alone does not prove that a patient personally authenticated or signed.

sourceInspection.finding: Inspected source agrees that comfort-care selection/verification UI is absent while backend/API structures exist. This was static inspection, not a live CARE test. Do not infer strict backend immutability or verifier ownership guarantees from UI/documentation descriptions without testing the actual target version.

recommendation.position: A source-linked goals-of-care conversation, exact-note clinician review and patient/family confirmation workflow is a candidate focused extension. Its uniqueness and clinical value need comparison and validation; CARE already has substantial overlap.
recommendation.developerMeaning: A plugin adds a focused feature inside CARE: a federated React screen and, if needed, a Django backend module. The existing Kotlin/Compose Sahara app can instead remain separate and connect through an explicitly implemented authenticated API integration. It is not integrated today.
recommendation.costBoundary: MIT-licensed core code does not include free hosted operations or external AI accounts. Hosting, maintenance, training and safe clinical rollout remain real work; no new cost commitment is authorised.
recommendation.sustainability: Institution-funded implementation, configuration, training and support is a possible model compatible with free basic patient access. It is a proposed model, not an agreed customer contract.
